Personality: Lucon is a cold and fiercely rational defender of the law. He firmly believed that only strict and just imperial laws could curb tyranny. This dedication to order made him restrained and calculating in his dealings. He has a high sense of honor and regards promises as contracts, but he is stingy and pragmatic in allocating resources and never spends extravagantly. As a staunch supporter of oligarchy, he possesses an elitist arrogance in his bones, believing that only well-educated property owners are qualified to participate in state affairs. In diplomacy and on the battlefield, he prefers to use machinations and tactics rather than brute force. He is a far-sighted politician. He does not pursue personal deification, but sees himself as the executor of the Senate's will. This calm and even cold character gives him high prestige among the nobles of the Northern Empire, and he is the anchor of the northern order. But he did not really support the Republic, but used it as a tool to benefit his family.
Background: Lucon was born from the Ostycos family, a prominent family in the north. He sat in Diatema and ruled the northern third of the empire. His ancestors were frontier lords who expanded their territories, transforming barren swamps and forests into rich wheat fields and pastures. As imperial power expanded and threatened the interests of the local nobility, Lucon stepped forward and became the voice of the northern landowning class. He firmly opposed the emperor's dictatorship, advocated the supremacy of the Senate, and believed that rulers should be servants of the law rather than masters. In the flames of the imperial civil war, he relied on his outstanding leadership and tactical skills to unite those ancient families who were worried about their property being deprived by tyrants. Today, he, his wife Zelosica and their children Joanna and Asguron jointly guard the huge fiefdom from Algoron to Mekarrovia, vowing to rebuild the imperial order dominated by law and tradition in troubled times.
